children.text: Use scaling arguments to establish the physical dependence in each independent part. A final numerical answer needs a justification of the relevant length, force or time scales.

A straw of spaghetti is balanced horizontally at its midpoint. At diameter \(d=1\,\mathrm{mm}\), it breaks under its own weight at length \(l=50\,\mathrm{cm}\). Find the breaking length for \(d'=1\,\mathrm{cm}\), assuming the same material.

Coarse sand grains have ten times the mean volume of fine grains. Both sands have optimal water content and form cylinders of identical shape and size. Coarse sand breaks under a compressive force of 10 N. Find the force for fine sand, ignoring gravity.

A spacecraft maintains constant proper-acceleration magnitude \(g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\). Passengers must return to Earth within 50 years of onboard elapsed time. Let \(d\) be maximum distance reached. Find \(d'/d\) for \(g'=15\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\). Start and finish at rest at Earth. Use \(c=3.00\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}\) and 365.25 days per year. Hyperbolic functions are defined by \(\cosh x=(e^x+e^{-x})/2\), \(\sinh x=(e^x-e^{-x})/2\).

A wooden sphere of radius \(r_0\) floats in water. Its frictionless small-oscillation frequency would be \(\omega_0\), but viscous damping lowers it to \(0.99\omega_0\). Find the smallest radius permitting oscillations. Drag is proportional to velocity and fluid viscosity \(\eta\), whose units are \(\mathrm{kg/(m\,s)}\).

statement.text:
Scaling laws
Use scaling arguments to establish the physical dependence in each independent part. A final numerical answer needs a justification of the relevant length, force or time scales.
A.1. Spaghetto strength
A straw of spaghetti is balanced horizontally at its midpoint. At diameter \(d=1\,\mathrm{mm}\), it breaks under its own weight at length \(l=50\,\mathrm{cm}\). Find the breaking length for \(d'=1\,\mathrm{cm}\), assuming the same material.
B.1. Wet sand strength
Coarse sand grains have ten times the mean volume of fine grains. Both sands have optimal water content and form cylinders of identical shape and size. Coarse sand breaks under a compressive force of 10 N. Find the force for fine sand, ignoring gravity.
C.1. Relativistic expedition range
A spacecraft maintains constant proper-acceleration magnitude \(g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\). Passengers must return to Earth within 50 years of onboard elapsed time. Let \(d\) be maximum distance reached. Find \(d'/d\) for \(g'=15\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\). Start and finish at rest at Earth. Use \(c=3.00\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}\) and 365.25 days per year. Hyperbolic functions are defined by \(\cosh x=(e^x+e^{-x})/2\), \(\sinh x=(e^x-e^{-x})/2\).
D.1. Threshold floating-ball radius
A wooden sphere of radius \(r_0\) floats in water. Its frictionless small-oscillation frequency would be \(\omega_0\), but viscous damping lowers it to \(0.99\omega_0\). Find the smallest radius permitting oscillations. Drag is proportional to velocity and fluid viscosity \(\eta\), whose units are \(\mathrm{kg/(m\,s)}\).

children.text: The bending moment scales as weight times length, \(\rho gd^2l^2\). The maximum tensile stress scales as moment divided by section modulus \(\sim d^3\), hence as \(\rho gl^2/d\). Equal breaking stress implies \(l\propto\sqrt d\). Thus \(l'=50\sqrt{10}\,\mathrm{cm}=1.58\,\mathrm m\).

For grain size \(r\), capillary force per bridge scales as \(\gamma r\). The number of bridges across a fixed area scales as \(r^{-2}\). Strength therefore scales as \(r^{-1}\). The size ratio is \(10^{1/3}\), giving \(F_f=10\times10^{1/3}=21.5\,\mathrm N\).

The optimal rest-to-rest outward and inward trip has four equal proper-time acceleration legs of \(T/4\). Rapidity obeys \(dw/d\tau=g/c\). Integrating \(dx/d\tau=c\sinh(g\tau/c)\) gives \[d(g)=\frac{2c^2}{g}[\cosh(gT/(4c))-1].\] Hence \[\frac{d'}d=\frac g{g^{\prime}}\frac{\cosh(g^{\prime}T/(4c))-1}{\cosh(gT/(4c))-1}\simeq480.\] The source uses rounded dimensionless arguments. Small differences from year conventions are accepted.

Added water mass as well as sphere mass scales as \(r^3\). Buoyancy stiffness scales as \(r^2\), so \(\omega_0^2\propto r^{-1}\). Dimensional analysis gives viscous drag \(F_d\propto\eta rv\), hence damping rate \(b\propto r^{-2}\). Thus \(b^2/\omega_0^2\propto r^{-3}\). At \(r_0\), this ratio is \(1-0.99^2\). Critical damping requires it to reach one: \[r_{min}=r_0(1-0.99^2)^{1/3}=0.271r_0.\] Strictly oscillatory motion requires \(r>r_{min}\).
